cases.title: The museum cat

item.description: The city museum posts a photo of an ancient Egyptian cat mummy.

clues.A: The city museum’s official account posted it.
clues.B: The museum’s website lists it in its collection with a catalog number.
clues.C: The wrappings look oddly perfect, almost like a printed pattern.
clues.D: The post names the gallery room and says it returned from repair last month.
clues.E: Someone asks how old it is. The museum replies with an age and links the collection page.

cases.lesson: Something can look too neat and still be real. A museum’s own records beat how it looks.

fib.right: Rats. I thought the neat wrapping would fool you.
fib.wrong: Ha! Real cat mummy. Its catalog number was right there.

cases.title: The robot cleaner

item.description: A post says a 6th grader built a robot that cleans a whole school in an hour.

clues.A: A page called Kid Genius News, created two weeks ago.
clues.B: No school or local paper mentions it.
clues.C: The robot looks real, but the school sign behind it has letters that don’t spell anything.
clues.D: It never names the student, the school or the town.
clues.E: Comments ask which school. The page posts another amazing kid story instead.

cases.lesson: A story that can’t be traced to a real person or place is a warning sign.

fib.right: Ugh. Scrambled letters on the sign. My weakness.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! No name, no school, no town. You believed a ghost.

cases.title: The book report

item.description: A classmate’s paragraph about the novel your class just read.

clues.A: Your classmate Jordan turned it in.
clues.B: A study site has a paragraph with almost the same sentences.
clues.C: The writing is smooth, but it gets the main character’s sister’s name wrong.
clues.D: It never mentions anything from your class discussion of the ending.
clues.E: The teacher asks Jordan about his point. He can’t explain it.

cases.lesson: A real writer can explain their own ideas. Wrong details about a book you both read are a big clue.

fib.right: Hmph. The wrong sister’s name gave me away.
fib.wrong: Ha! He couldn’t explain his own paragraph, and you missed it.

cases.title: The frozen bubble

item.description: A soap bubble freezes into ice crystals that spread across it like a special effect.

clues.A: A weather reporter at your local TV station posted it.
clues.B: Many people in cold places have posted videos of the same thing.
clues.C: The crystals spread so perfectly it looks fake.
clues.D: She says it was well below freezing that morning and her kids blew the bubbles.
clues.E: Asked how, she explains: bubble soap, very cold air and no wind.

cases.lesson: Nature can look like special effects. Many separate videos of the same thing is good evidence.

fib.right: Fine. Frozen bubbles are real. I hoped you didn’t know.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! Real bubble. Half the internet has filmed one.

cases.title: The friendly new player

item.description: A new player called Nova compliments everyone in your game server.

clues.A: The account was made yesterday and has no profile picture.
clues.B: The exact message “Love your builds, you’re so talented!” went to 40 players.
clues.C: Perfect spelling, and replies within a second, day and night.
clues.D: Nova never mentions anything specific about the game you’re playing together.
clues.E: You ask what Nova built last week. Nova changes the subject to a link for free coins.

cases.lesson: Bots can act friendly. Copy-paste compliments plus a link are a warning sign: don’t click, and tell an adult.

fib.right: Rats. Forty players, same compliment. Lazy of me.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! Nova’s a bot. You almost clicked my link.

cases.title: Grandma’s recipe card

item.description: A stained, faded handwritten recipe card for cornbread, shared in your family group chat.

clues.C: Some words are smudged, and one amount is crossed out and rewritten.
clues.D: Your uncle says it was in Grandma’s kitchen drawer and she always doubled the butter.
clues.E: You ask your mom. She remembers the same card.

cases.lesson: Someone you trust who remembers it is strong evidence.

fib.right: Bah. Your mom remembered the card.
fib.wrong: Ha! Real card. Your own mom could have told you.

cases.title: The famous quote

item.description: A quote site says a famous inventor once said, “Failure is just success that hasn’t been tagged yet.”

clues.A: A quote site with no author and no sources.
clues.B: The quote appears in no book, speech or interview you can find.
clues.D: It gives no date, book or speech it came from.
clues.E: You email for the source. An automatic reply says quotes are “curated by our system.”

cases.lesson: Real quotes can be traced to where they were said. If nobody can find the source, don’t use it.

fib.right: Ugh. No source, no quote. You’re learning.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! Nobody ever said that. I made it up.

cases.title: Toast the lizard

item.description: The school website shows the class bearded dragon wearing a tiny party hat.

clues.A: The science teacher posted it on the school’s official website.
clues.B: The same lizard is in last year’s yearbook.
clues.C: The hat looks a bit fake and the lighting is strange.
clues.D: The post names the lizard, Toast, and says it was his fifth birthday.
clues.E: You ask the teacher. She shows you the hat in her desk drawer.

cases.lesson: Strange lighting isn’t proof. Ask someone who was there.

fib.wrong: Ha! Toast is real, and so is the hat.

cases.title: The glowing frog

item.description: A short video shows a “newly discovered” glowing blue frog in a rainforest.

clues.A: A channel that posts a new “discovered animal” every day.
clues.B: No science site or museum mentions the frog.
clues.C: In one frame, the frog’s toes blend into the leaf.
clues.D: It never names the scientists or the country.
clues.E: Comments ask where. The channel pins “Nature is amazing!”
clues.F: The description says “Made with creative tools.”

cases.lesson: Real discoveries are reported by named scientists in named places. Vague wording like “creative tools” can be a quiet label.

fib.right: Rats. You read the fine print.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! A new animal every day? That should have tipped you off.

cases.title: The thank-you card

item.description: Your lab partner gives you a typed thank-you card with perfect spelling and polished sentences.

clues.A: Your lab partner Priya gave it to you in class.
clues.C: The spelling is perfect and the sentences are very polished.
clues.D: It mentions the exact moment your volcano overflowed onto the teacher’s shoes.
clues.E: You ask her about it. She says her older sister helped fix her spelling.

cases.lesson: Polished writing isn’t proof of AI. Details only someone who was there would know matter more.

fib.right: Bah. I bet on the perfect spelling.
fib.wrong: Ha! Priya wrote it. Nobody else knew about the shoes.
